capabilities.summary: This session targets a real device, so simulator-only boot/install helpers are not part of its contract.
details: Retry on a simulator target if you need simulator log capture or fixture build/install helpers.

capabilities.summary: Probe opened a live real-device runner session through explicit devicectl, signing, and XCUITest transport validation.
details: xcrun devicectl device info apps --device 00008110-0006293936C0401E --bundle-id com.skastr0.ripple --json-output <path>
xcrun devicectl device process launch --device 00008110-0006293936C0401E --terminate-existing com.skastr0.ripple --json-output <path>

capabilities.summary: The real-device runner is live over a device-specific bootstrap-manifest + HTTP POST + stdout-ready transport.
details: Command ingress uses the runner-local HTTP listener reported in the ready frame.
Ready-state events are still parsed from stdout JSONL frames embedded in the mixed xcodebuild/XCTest log stream.
Runner feature flags such as uiAction and uiActionBatch are reported under session health runner details.

capabilities.summary: Perf recording can attach xctrace to the live real-device target pid exposed by the runner session.
details: Real-device xctrace recording still depends on the live runner pid and connected-device availability.

capabilities.summary: Real-device sessions expose build + runner boundary artifacts, but there is no long-lived device unified-log collector yet.
details: You can inspect the saved xcodebuild-session, wrapper stderr, stdout-event, and preflight artifacts through session logs or artifact drill.
Real-device live unified logging remains an explicit later seam.

capabilities.summary: Device-session LLDB attach is still outside the verified contract for this slice.
details: The only verified persistent debugger path today is the external host-process bridge.

shown: Real-device runner control uses the honest XCUITest boundary seam for device sessions: bootstrap manifest plus HTTP POST ingress plus stdout-framed mixed-log ready egress.
Device reconnects are surfaced explicitly in session health; Probe does not claim transparent recovery of real-device runner state.
Session cleanup is daemon-owned; close/session shutdown tears down the runner wrapper process group and removes the bootstrap manifest.
